rationale.text: The test applies to each bitmap image (<canvas>) that has an adjacent caption, and asks four conditions, all of them: the image and caption in a figure, a role attribute of figure or group on the figure, an aria-label on the figure identical to the caption, and the caption in a figcaption. Each is a requirement. The glossary gives one exception, which explains "si nécessaire": when the adjacent text can serve as the image's replacement text, the figure and figcaption set is not required and the image can be treated as decorative. It is listed on each requirement. Which images have a caption is judgment in general: a caption is adjacent text that informs about or completes the image, and code cannot recognise one outside a figcaption. So no check resolves any requirement, conditions 1 and 4 have no link, and the entry is below full. One case is mechanical. A figure that holds only the image and one figcaption with text is a captioned image under any reading: the glossary names figure and figcaption as the way HTML associates a caption, and says an image without a caption is one outside a figure or in a figure without figcaption. For such a pair two custom checks examine the second and third conditions. One faults a figure with no role attribute, or with one token other than figure or group: the wording asks for the attribute, and technical note 1 explains it is there because figure elements are not supported, so the element's implicit role does not stand in for it. The other faults a figure with no aria-label, an aria-label without letters or numbers, or one whose letters and numbers differ from those of a plain-text figcaption: technical note 1 says using a figcaption imposes at least an aria-label with identical content, and technical note 3 rules out aria-labelledby. Both abstain on the exception's cases: a witness image must be exposed, visible, with no empty alt, no presentational role and a name with letters or numbers, so it is not treated as decorative, and the exception as the glossary words it needs an image treated as decorative. They also abstain on images or captions that are hidden, invisible or off-screen, on a figure holding anything else or a figcaption holding a control, on images using aria-labelledby or aria-describedby, and on frames and shadow trees. Each examines both routes and the exception of its requirement, so its fault means failure; its scope is partial, because captioned images outside a figure with figcaption are never examined. The checks never answer no_fault, so the entry is fail_only. No axe-core rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment, because whether any image on the page has a caption is judgment. Needs is empty: attributes, styles, geometry and the accessibility tree are read on the page as loaded.
